links.outcome: Change in CAN algorithm performance (PPV, F1, FPR, NPV) over time, 2016-2021
links.effect: PPV decreased 4.0% (95% CI -2.8% to -5.1%); F1 decreased 4.6%; FPR increased 0.34%, corresponding to 18,288 additional false positives; TPR and accuracy stable.
links.quote: From 2016 to 2021, PPV decreased by 4.0% (95% CI, -2.8% to -5.1%); F1 score decreased by 4.6% (95% CI, -6.1% to 3.0%); NPV increased by 0.43% (95% CI, 0.30% to 0.57%); and FPR increased by 0.34% (95% CI, 0.10% to 0.58%), which corresponds with 18 288 increased false positive results.

links.outcome: Loss of accuracy relative to initial performance in a deployed national model
links.effect: Performance declined 2016-2021 from shifts in outcome prevalence and covariates: PPV fell 4.0%, F1 fell 4.6%, FPR rose; event rate fell from 3.8% (2017) to 3.0% (2021).
links.quote: This cohort study found that CAN algorithm performance declined from 2016 to 2021 due to shifts in outcome prevalence and distributions of health care utilization and demographic covariates.

links.outcome: Covariate shift and quality metric false positive rate drift in deployed algorithm
links.effect: Covariate shifts in 19 covariates; FPR among metric-eligible veterans rose from 81.6% in 2018 to 85.7% in 2020 for the palliative care quality metric.
links.quote: Covariate shifts were observed in 19 covariates, with demographic characteristics, health care utilization, and laboratory covariates exhibiting the largest shifts.

screen.reason: Evaluates performance drift and clinical consequences in an already nationally deployed risk algorithm (VA CAN), but does not test or compare an intervention or safeguard practice (it measures drift rather than testing a specific monitoring or mitigation practice).
